qt: to the Commission António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Tiago Moreira de Sá (PfE), Gerolf Annemans (PfE), Fabrice Leggeri (PfE), Petr Bystron (ESN), Tom Vandendriessche (PfE), Markus Buchheit (ESN), Elisabeth Dieringer (PfE), Isabella Tovaglieri (PfE), Volker Schnurrbusch (ESN), Silvia Sardone (PfE), Dominik Tarczyński (ECR), Petras Gražulis (ESN), Marc Jongen (ESN), Branko Grims (NI), Alvise Pérez (NI), Virginie Joron (PfE), Balázs Orbán (PfE), Enikő Győri (PfE), András László (PfE), Christine Anderson (ESN), Zsuzsanna Borvendég (ESN), Catherine Griset (PfE) Subject:

At the Patriots Academy event that took place in Ericeira between 25 and 27 September 2026, amid a heavy police presence, MEPs, national MPs, hundreds of young Europeans and other attendees were taunted and labelled ‘pigs’, ‘fascists’ and ‘Nazis’ by protesters affiliated with anti-fascist movements1. This was not an isolated incident. In February 2026, a 23-year-old man named Quentin Deranque died after being assaulted in Lyon2. The suspects had links to anti-fascist groups. In September 2026, professor Damien Ernst was attacked by a group of masked individuals while teaching a class at the University of Liège3. In the light of Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union: 1.

What steps will the Commission take, under the aegis of the European Democracy Shield and the forthcoming recommendation on the safety of political actors, and regardless of the perpetrators’ ideological leanings, to protect elected representatives and people involved in politics and democratic life, including young people, from violence and intimidation?

Having regard to Article 138(1)(c)(vi) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 and the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES), what steps is the Commission taking to exclude from EU funding organisations that incite hatred or political violence, and what checks is it carrying out on existing beneficiaries?
